newsitem.title: FRANCE: French AOM airline may get new executive -paper.
newsitem.headline: French AOM airline may get new executive -paper.

text.p: French private airline AOM, owned by the state-backed CDR holding company, appeared likely to get a managing director in the near future, to prepare the sale of the company, newspaper Le Monde reported.

"A compromise solution seems to have been reached, with the highly probable appointment of a managing director 'responsible for future contacts with the CDR,' the newspaper reported in its Sunday edition.
The Consortium de Realisation handles sales of assets formerly held by the distressed Credit Lyonnais bank, which include AOM.
The new executive, who would "prepare the sale of AOM," would be a compromise solution following the CDR's criticisms of AOM chairman Alexandre Couvelaire, the newspaper said.
Despite the criticisms, aides to Prime Minister Alain Juppe and President Jacques Chirac maintained their support for Couvelaire at a meeting last Thursday, it said.

The CDR representative believes Couvelaire failed in the task of building a strong French private sector airline when he let British Airways gain sole bidding for the insovent Air Liberte company, which will give valuable landing rights to BA.
AOM specialises in domestic flights and routes to French territories and departments overseas.
AOM is expected to post a 1996 loss of around 180 million francs after a 27 million profit last year, the report said.
French newspapers report Air France is interested in buying AOM to protect its airport hub, and the Nouvelles Frontieres travel agency has said it is in talks with CDR to acquire AOM.
